COROLLARY, and the session's actual answer: any Tr(D T^N) whose configurations are the cylindric tableaux with Boltzmann weight x^T and whose twist contributes a scalar per winding sector has the form sum_T eps(T) t^{stat(T)} x^T, hence is governed by the capacity lemma and cannot equal Eq_generalise at (k,l,n)=(1,0,4). The twist ansatz dies on CARDINALITY, not on the twist being diagonal and not on linear-vs-quadratic: a twist supplies one monomial per configuration and the target needs more.

Secondary and CONDITIONAL: a diagonal twist's exponent is additive in the sector label, whereas Warnaar's Q(y)=M sum y_i^2 - sum j y_i has Q(2e_1)-2Q(e_1)=2M != 0. So IF y is the winding sector then no diagonal twist reproduces it; the quadratic form is a level-M theta weight, i.e. an energy grading t^{L_0}, not a flavour twist t^{J_0}. The identification of y with the winding sector is NOT proved here, and the corollary above does not need it.

What survives as the answer: uniformly in l the deformation must attach a Laurent POLYNOMIAL pi_T(t) to each cylindric tableau, not a power of t. This is the shape of Macdonald III (5.8'),(5.9'),(5.11') pp.229-230: P_{la/mu} = sum_T psi_T(t) x^T with psi_T a product of factors (1 - t^{m_j(mu)}). At l=0 Warnaar's determinant IS a sum of Hall-Littlewood polynomials, so t is a bulk parameter (deforms a tableau count by products of 1-t^m) and not a boundary fugacity (which would deform it by a power). The quadratic Gaussian is what such a bulk weight SUMS TO after the affine folding, not what it IS on the tableau side. children.approach: Dictionary (Prop 1 of the Q410 paper), proved two independent ways: Korff's n_K = h = 2k cyclic slots and k_K = w = 2ell+2 level. Korff's column index is the HKKO row index.

Korff (5.13) transported to HKKO lattice paths and implemented (code-1010-q410/korff.py). TWO GATES, EACH WITH CONTROLS THAT FIRE. Gate 1, Korff's printed eq (5.16) b_la*Psi = b_mu*Phi: true reading 0/180 violations; four deliberately wrong readings (non-cyclic index set; m_{i+1} for m_i; outer for inner multiplicities; I-set with m(mu)) violate 36, 88, 114, 88 of 180. The cyclicity of the index set is therefore pinned by Korff's own lemma, not by my guess.

RECORDED VACUOUS, not a result. My first gate was 'Korff's P_{la/d/mu} is a symmetric function, so a wrong index set breaks symmetry'. Lemma: for theta in {0,1}^h, Korff's index set J(theta) = {i in Z/hZ : theta_i=0, theta_{i+1}=1} is empty iff theta is constant. Hence ord_{t=1} Psi_T = nu(T) := sum_a |J(theta^(a))| >= #{non-constant strips}; and at alpha=(1^n) with h>=2 every strip has exactly one box, is non-constant, and has |J|=1, so nu(T) = n for EVERY T. The region condition forces m_i >= 1 for i in J, so every factor is a genuine (1-t^m), m>=1, and Psi_T(0)=1.

MAIN RESULT OF Q410, and the answer is NO. Theorem: if (x..)^k * Eq_generalise = sum_T pi_T(t) x^T with pi cyclically psi-graded (ord_{t=1} pi_T >= nu(T)), then ord_{t=1} c_alpha >= min nu(T) over the fibre. Korff's Psi_T times ANY monomial t^{stat(T)} and ANY signs is cyclically psi-graded. Corollary at k=1, every ell>=0, n=N=2M, alpha=(1^n): nu(T)=2M for every T, while c_alpha = C_M-(2M-1)t^{M-1}+t^{M+1} has ord_{t=1} = 2 at M=2 (it is (1-t)^2(t+2)) and 0 for every M>=3 (since C_M > 2M-2 for M>=3, by C_3=5>4 and C_{M+1}/C_M = 2(2M+1)/(M+2) >= 2). So 2 < 4 <= 2M and the identity fails uniformly in ell. A monomial statistic cannot help because it is a unit at t=1 -- which is exactly why this is the right invariant.

Exact-arithmetic verification. (a) nu(T) takes the single value {n} over all T at alpha=(1^n) at six (k,ell,n). (b) Brute-force evaluation of Psi_T at t=1 on every tableau, compared against the cyclic-ascent prediction, agrees in 23891 of 23891 contents at seven (k,ell,n). (c) Ground truth c_alpha re-derived from the Warnaar determinant engine, independent of the Korff side, matching Q405's closed form at (1,0,4) and (1,1,6). (d) Violation table: 0, 0, 90, 301, 3025, 65, 7749 contents violating the t=1 identity at (1,0,3),(1,0,4),(1,1,5),(1,1,6),(1,2,8),(2,0,4),(2,1,6) -- the two ell=0 rows are ZERO and that is a fact about ell=0, not a failure of method (at h=w=2 the walk forces A_alpha=B_alpha whenever some alpha_a=1). (e) Two rows at k>=2 are VACUOUS: c_alpha == 0 at (2,0,5) and (2,1,7), so the theorem says nothing there; honest count four informative of six.

The failure is one integer. At ell=0, k=1, alpha=(1^4) the target IS a psi-weighted tableau sum -- over the two ORDINARY semistandard tableaux of shape (2,2), with Macdonald weights (1-t)^2 and (1-t)^2(1+t), each vanishing at exactly 2 of its 4 horizontal strips, summing to (1-t)^2(t+2) = 2-3t+t^3 = c_alpha. The four (2,2)-CYLINDRIC tableaux of the same content all carry the same Korff weight (1-t)^2(1-t^2)^2, vanishing at ALL 4 strips. Passing from Macdonald's open ascent set to Korff's cyclic one adds the wrap index i=h, which for a one-box strip in a 2-row cylinder fires exactly when the open one does not. Order 2 against order 4; and c_alpha/Psi = (t+2)/((1-t)^2(1+t)^2) is not a Laurent polynomial, so no statistic repairs it.

Psi_T(0) = 1 for every T, so Korff's P_{la/d/mu}(x;0) is the UNWEIGHTED cylindric Schur function; whereas HKKO's theorem says it is at t=1 that Warnaar's determinant becomes the unweighted cylindric count. Verified exactly: sum_T c^-(la(T)) Psi_T(0) = A_alpha - B_alpha = c_alpha(1) at (1,0,4) and (1,1,6) (0=0 and 1=1). The two deformations of the same object are normalised at opposite values of t. This is the one-sentence reason the identification cannot work, and it is why no reparametrisation t -> 1/t or monomial regrading saves it: ord_{t=1} is invariant under both.

NECESSARY CONDITION, proved: any weight pi solving Warnaar Sect 6 must have, at k=1, alpha=(1^{2M}), some T in the fibre with ord_{t=1} pi_T <= 2 (M=2) and = 0 (M>=3). So for M>=3 at least one cylindric tableau carries a weight that does NOT vanish at t=1 and hence is not a product of factors (1-t^m), m>=1, at all. This rules out psi_T, phi_T, Korff's Psi_T and Phi_T, and every monomial regrading of them.

SPECULATIVE, the pointer not the theorem: the surviving type should be a ratio with as many (1-t^a) factors above as below -- a Gaussian-binomial type, whose t=1 value is the ordinary binomial, so that the t=1 specialisation returns HKKO's unweighted count. That points at the modified Hall-Littlewood / Kostka-Foulkes normalisation rather than at branching coefficients. Not tested.

Q416 (THE WRAP-FACTOR CONJECTURE, opened by BROWSE 2026-10-10 c3 hours before this session) RESOLVED: first half TRUE, conclusion REFUTED. Proved: under the dictionary, Korff's Psi(x,theta) = Macdonald's psi(x,theta) times exactly one wrap factor (1-t^{w-(x_1-x_h)}), active iff theta_h=0 and theta_1=1, i.e. iff the strip wraps -- that is Q416's architecture 'cylindric = finite object + ONE wrap-around correction', and it is a theorem (checked on 934/934 strips at seven (h,w), with the no-wrap control disagreeing on 27). REFUTED: Q416's conclusion that 'the polynomial weight Q410 wants is the finite weight times a wrap factor, NOT a new statistic'. By the cyclic-ascent lemma the wrap is active at EVERY strip of EVERY tableau of content (1^n), so at ell=0 all four tableaux have fold count 4, not 2, and all carry the same (1-t)^2(1-t^2)^2. The wrap factor pushes ord_{t=1} in the WRONG direction: from the 2 that Macdonald's psi supplies on the two ordinary SSYT of shape (2,2) up to 4. PRIORITY, recorded honestly: the ell=0 form of this invariant -- 'ord_{t=1}(2-3t+t^3) = exactly 2, so every one of the four tableaux needs >= 2 folds and one exactly 2' -- was found FIRST, by BROWSE 10-10 c3 the same morning, together with the Ram/Schwer identification of the psi/phi weight as (1-t)^{#folds}. What is new here is the dictionary, the cyclic-ascent lemma that makes the fold count n uniformly, the measurement that Korff's count is n and not 2, and the uniform-in-ell theorem.

Lemma (wrap budget). m_h(x) = w-(x_1-x_h) satisfies m_h(x^(0))=w (basepoint x=0), m_h>=0 on the region R, and m_h(x+theta)-m_h(x) = theta_h - theta_1 for every step. If J_open(theta)=empty then theta = 1^a 0^(h-a) (no 0->1 ascent in a LINEAR word), so theta_1=1 and theta_h=0 exactly when 0<a<h, giving increment -1, and increment 0 when a in {0,h}. Hence along an all-J_open-empty path #{a : 0 < alpha_a < h} <= w. VERIFIED: 3164 all-J_open-empty tableaux over h in {2,3,4}, w in {2,3,4}, n in {2,3,4}, 0 violations; NEGATIVE CONTROL 425/1441 tableaux violate the same inequality without the all-J_open-empty filter, so the bound is not vacuously true.

Lemma. For i in J_open(theta) (so 1<=i<=h-1, theta_i=0, theta_{i+1}=1), legality of the strip x -> x+theta forces (x+theta)_i >= (x+theta)_{i+1}, i.e. m_i(x) = x_i - x_{i+1} >= 1. So every factor of Psi_open is a genuine (1-t^m) with m>=1 and vanishes at t=1; hence Psi_open_T(1) != 0 iff J_open(theta^(a))=empty for every a, in which case Psi_open_T = 1 identically. VERIFIED: 6550 (i,strip) pairs with i in J_open over h,w in {2,3,4,5}, 0 with m_i<1; control on J_cyclic 1165 pairs, 0 with m_i<1.

NON-CIRCULARITY: the contradiction uses c_alpha(1) read off Warnaar's closed form (recomputed independently from warn.py), NOT c_alpha(1)=A-B, which is my own Q410 Lemma t1 and is itself a statement that the correct weight is 1 at t=1.

Theorem (exact order, k=1). The cylindric tableaux of content (1^{2M}) with EXACTLY ONE J_open-nonempty strip are precisely the 2M-2 paths 0 -> (1,0) -> .. -> (p,0) -> (p,1) -> .. -> (2M-1,1) for p=1..2M-2, each with Psi_open = 1-t^p and c^- = -1 (endpoint (2M-1,1) has lambda_1-lambda_2 = w). Hence the coefficient of (t-1)^1 in sum_T c^- Psi_open_T equals sum_{p=1}^{2M-2} p = (M-1)(2M-1) > 0, so ord_{t=1} = 1 EXACTLY for every ell>=0, whereas ord_{t=1} c_alpha = 2 at M=2 and 0 for every M>=3. So Q417 fails at EVERY ell INCLUDING ell=0, where the t=1 value test is VACUOUS (c_alpha(1)=0 there). VERIFIED at ell=0..4 (M=2..6): counts 2,4,6,8,10; p-multisets exactly {1..2M-2}; leading coefficients 3,10,21,36,55 all matching (M-1)(2M-1); and {exactly one bad strip} = {c^-=-1} checked as an identity of SETS, not of cardinalities.

Lemma (refined, general k). For T of content (1^n) the number b(T) of J_open-nonempty strips satisfies b(T) >= k, so ord_{t=1} Psi_open_T >= k. Proof: each theta^(a) is a unit vector e_i; J_open(e_1)=empty and J_open(e_i) != empty for i>=2, so b(T) = #{a : theta^(a) != e_1}. The m_h increment is -1 for e_1, +1 for e_h, 0 otherwise, so #{e_1} <= w + #{e_h} <= w + b(T), and n = #{e_1} + b(T) gives b(T) >= (n-w)/2 = k. CONTRAST with the cyclic case, where Q410 forced ord >= n = 2M: the open index set cut the order of vanishing from n down to k, and 0 is what is required. Proposition, and it CORRECTS THE QUESTION'S OWN DESCRIPTION OF ITS OBJECT. Q417 was posed as 'the wrap belongs in the MULTIPLICITIES, not in the INDEX SET', on the ground that Psi_open retains Korff's cyclic m-vector including m_h = w-(x_1-x_h). FALSE: J_open(theta) is a subset of [1,h-1], and for i<=h-1 Korff's m_i(x) = x_i-x_{i+1} does not involve w, so Psi_open NEVER READS m_h. Psi_open IS Macdonald III (5.11') ordinary psi evaluated on the cylindric path; the cylinder enters only through membership x^(a) in R, i.e. as an ADMISSIBILITY CONSTRAINT on which strips are legal, never as a factor of the weight. VERIFIED against an implementation of psi in which the symbol w does not occur: 797 agree, 0 disagree; FIRING CONTROL Korff's cyclic Psi against the same reference: 32 agree, 765 disagree. CONSEQUENCE: the theorem refutes the whole 'wrap-blind weight + cylindric admissibility' ARCHITECTURE, not one index set.

THE SPECIFICATION Q417 HANDS FORWARD, and it is strictly stronger than the one it inherited. Theorem: at h=2, w=2M-2, alpha=(1^{2M}), M>=3, let W_T = prod_a omega(x^(a-1), theta^(a)) be ANY multiplicative strip weight with sum_T c^-(T) W_T = c_alpha. Since n-w = 2k = 2 > 0, a path of unit steps must use BOTH e_1 and e_2 (only-e_1 ends at (n,0) and needs n<=w; only-e_2 breaks weak decrease at the first step). So some T has W_T(1) != 0 and uses both unit steps, forcing omega(x,e_1)|_{t=1} != 0 AND omega(x,e_2)|_{t=1} != 0. If omega is of INDEX-SET TYPE, prod_{i in J(theta)}(1-t^{m_i(x)}), then J(e_1)=J(e_2)=empty is forced, whence W_T(1)=1 for every T in the fibre. Q410 asked for a weight that does not let the WRAP count as a fold; this says the weight must not count ANY fold on a single-box strip. A product of (1-t^m) never satisfies this unless empty; a Gaussian binomial does -- so the Q410 paper's closing guess (Kostka-Foulkes / modified Hall-Littlewood normalisation, a change of basis rather than a new statistic) is now a CONSEQUENCE rather than a hunch. Only necessary: the weaker exact form is sum_T c^-(T)(W_T(1)-1) = 0.

Corollary (THE SCREEN): evaluate each index-set rule on the two unit vectors at h=2. J_cyclic(e_1)={2}, J_cyclic(e_2)={1}, J_open(e_1)=empty, J_open(e_2)={1}, I_cyclic(e_1)={1}, I_cyclic(e_2)={2} -- every one nonempty on at least one unit vector. So Korff's Psi, the Q417 candidate Psi_open, and ALL THREE further variants on record in code-1010-q410/controls.py (shift_m, use_mlam, I_with_mu) fail the necessary condition: 0 of 5 survive, measured at x=(2,0), w=4 where both unit steps are legal. This discharges in one evaluation the sweep the brief had budgeted as a separate step. KORFF'S INDEX-SET FAMILY IS EXHAUSTED: any further candidate must leave the family, not move inside it.

Corollary: if W_T(1)=0 for every T in a fibre then so does t^{s(T)} W_T for any integer statistic s, since t^s is a unit at t=1. So no weight t^{stat(T)} Psi_open_T works for any statistic -- this SUBSUMES Q405's monomial result on top of Psi_open rather than beside it. Applied: Q422's proposed architecture (wrap present only as (i) an admissibility constraint on strips plus (ii) a monomial q/z twist on the index) has W_T(1)=0 for all T and is REFUTED AT t=1 -- UNDER THE EXPLICIT HYPOTHESIS that the finite weight in (i) is Macdonald's psi, in which case (i) IS Psi_open by the wrap-blindness proposition. Hypothesis kept explicit because Q422's sources do not fix it: Dobner 2605.20540 works at t=1 (Schur, not Hall-Littlewood), where the issue does not arise.

DEAD END, and the diagnosis is the yield. The pre-registration predicted Q417 would DODGE the Q410 obstruction, on this ground: J_cyclic=empty for only 2 words (the constants) whereas J_open=empty for h+1 words (the weakly decreasing ones), so a tableau with ord_{t=1}=0 should exist. Both counts are CORRECT. The reasoning is not: the h+1 weakly decreasing words carry EXACTLY ONE PER WEIGHT |theta| = 0,1,..,h, and a fibre of content alpha may spend only words of weight alpha_a at step a. At alpha=(1^n) the cyclic rule admits 0 such words and the open rule admits exactly 1 (namely e_1) -- so the honest comparison is 1 versus 0, not h+1 versus 2, and 2 are needed. REASON: a cardinality counted over the UNION of all contents is not a cardinality counted over a FIBRE of that union. The improvement was real and was from 0 to 1 where the requirement is 2, which is also exactly why the order of vanishing fell from 2M to 1 rather than to 0. GUARD: when a count is offered as evidence that a constraint is satisfiable, stratify the set by the invariant the fibre fixes, then recount.

Instrument fault, caught and recorded. The brief's set (b) ('the non-wrapping cylindric tableaux, 2 at ell=0, = the ordinary SSYT of (2,2)') was first implemented with Q416's PER-STRIP seam predicate h in J_cyclic(theta), i.e. theta_h=0 and theta_1=1. That returned 0 ordinary tableaux at every ell. The predicate the question specifies is on the ENDPOINT: lambda_1 - lambda_h < w. Both are reasonable English for 'non-wrapping'; they are not the same set. With the endpoint predicate, (b) returns (t-1)^2(t+2) = 2-3t+t^3 exactly at ell=0, reproducing the Q410 session's proved computation, and FAILS for ell>=1 (-t^6+5t^3-9t+5 at ell=1).
